facts.statement: Paleontologists speculate that the damaged skull of the type specimen suggests the animal was involved in a fight before it died.
facts.quote: the skull is damaged, causing some paleontologists to speculate that it was involved in a fight prior to death.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Aucasaurus represents a mature individual that was at least eleven years old.
facts.quote: The type specimen belongs to a mature individual of at least eleven years old.

facts.statement: Aucasaurus was a medium-sized abelisaur measuring between 5.5 and 6.2 meters in length and weighing approximately 700 kilograms.
facts.quote: Aucasaurus was a medium-sized abelisaur, measuring 5.5 - 6.2 m long and weighing approximately 700 kg.

facts.statement: Instead of horns, Aucasaurus possessed a pair of low ridges located above each eye.
facts.quote: Instead of horns, it had a pair of low ridges above each eye.

facts.statement: The hand of Aucasaurus was unusual because it possessed four metacarpals, but the first and fourth lacked fingers.
facts.quote: The hand of Aucasaurus was unusual: four metacarpals were present, but the first and fourth lacked fingers.

facts.statement: Traits in the tail vertebrae suggest significant musculature and rigidity, possibly indicating that Aucasaurus was capable of running fast.
facts.quote: Traits found in the caudal vertebrae suggests a significant caudal musculature and rigidity, possibly indicating that it could have been a fast runner.

facts.statement: The fused tail vertebrae in Aucasaurus represent the earliest known occurrence of block vertebrae in the non-avian theropod fossil record.
facts.quote: This represents the earliest known occurrence of this pathology in the non-avian theropod fossil record.

facts.statement: Aucasaurus walked on two legs, with an estimated length of 7 meters, a height of 2.4 meters, and a weight of around 700 kg.
facts.quote: Aucasaurus caminaba de modo bípedo, su longitud estimada es de 7 metros y 2,4 de altura con un peso de alrededor 700 kg.

facts.statement: Because Aucasaurus fossils were found near a large sauropod egg nest, researchers believe it preyed on the hatchlings and juveniles there.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado junto a los restos de una importante nidada de saurópodos, por lo que se piensa que depredaba a las crías y jóvenes del lugar.

facts.statement: Like its relative, Aucasaurus possessed long and powerful hind limbs, suggesting it was a great runner.
facts.quote: Igual que este poseía miembros posteriores largos y poderosos, por lo que debió ser un gran corredor.

facts.statement: The Aucasaurus fossil was found in Campanian sediments of the Río Colorado Subgroup within the Anacleto Formation in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: El fósil de Aucasaurus se encontró en sedimentos del Campaniano pertenecientes al Subgrupo Río Colorado de la Formación Anacleto, en la Provincia del Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The new genus was named in 2002 by Rodolfo Coria, Luis Chiappe, and Lowell Dingus in a brief communication.
facts.quote: El nuevo género fue nombrado en 2002 por Rodolfo Coria, Luis Chiappe y Lowell Dingus, en una comunicación rápida.

facts.statement: The species name A. garridoi was given in honor of Mr. Alberto Garrido, who discovered the holotype.
facts.quote: La especie A. garridoi se le dio en homenaje al Sr. Alberto Garrido, que descubrió el holotipo.

facts.statement: The specimen shows impressions of soft tissue at the level of the pelvic region.
facts.quote: El espécimen muestra impresiones de tejido blando a la altura de la región pélvica.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed Aucasaurus garridoi to Abelisaurus garridoi.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed Aucasaurus garridoi into Abelisaurus garridoi.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies suggest Aucasaurus is more closely related to taxa like Carnotaurus, with some researchers including them in the Carnotaurini.
facts.quote: subsequent studies suggest that Aucasaurus was more closely related to other taxa such as Carnotaurus, with some including them in the Carnotaurini.

facts.statement: The genus Aucasaurus was named by Coria and colleagues in 2002.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Aucasaurus (genus), Coria et al. 2002

facts.statement: Aucasaurus belongs to the subgroup Brachyrostra.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachyrostra

facts.statement: Aucasaurus is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Aucasaurus is Aucasaurus garridoi.
facts.quote: Type species: Aucasaurus garridoi

facts.statement: Aucasaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Aucasaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
